newsitem.title: UK: Britain's August car sales race higher - report.
newsitem.headline: Britain's August car sales race higher - report.

text.p: Sales of new "R" registration cars in Britain have soared in the first few days of August, the first month of availability, newspapers reported on Thursday.
The Independent quoted figures from the industry's Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders (SMMT) showing 208,000 registrations were recorded in the first 10 days of the month.
No one at SMMT was immediately available for comment.
The Independent said the figures could mean the whole month would see record-breaking sales of "well over 500,000". Last August sales were 479,407.
The previous August peak was at 500,112 in 1989, the newspaper said.
The Independent said U.S. giant Ford's share of the market was 16 percent in the first 10 days.
The Daily Telegraph claimed even more buoyant figures of 282,000 registrations in just the first five selling days of the month.
It said imports accounted for 67 percent of the sales, compared with 62-63 percent a year ago.
The Daily Telegraph did not give a source for its figures.
